description:
OpenClaw's #1 problem: your agent forgets its instructions after context compaction. Here's the complete memory architecture that fixes it - from built-in settings most users never tune to advanced semantic search across your entire knowledge base.

Full guide with all configs and copy-paste templates: https://velvetshark.com/openclaw-memory-masterclass

I'm an OpenClaw maintainer. This is the guide I wish existed when I started. Everything here is based on public docs, open source code, and 2+ months of running this system daily.

What you'll learn:
- The 4 memory layers and 3 failure modes (diagnostic checklist)
- The pre-compaction memory flush most users never discover
- The /compact timing trick that gives new instructions maximum lifespan
- A file architecture that survives compaction by design
- Built-in hybrid search vs QMD for searching your entire knowledge base
- Why memory architecture also saves you money on API costs

---

Chapters:
0:00 - Meta's alignment director lost control of her agent
1:59 - Quick start: if you only do 3 things
3:01 - The 4 "memories" people confuse
4:52 - 3 failure modes: why your agent forgets
6:42 - Compaction vs pruning (completely different)
8:05 - Prove what's loaded: /context list
10:06 - What compaction actually does
13:42 - Layer 1: pre-compaction memory flush
16:27 - Layer 2: manual memory discipline + /compact trick
19:12 - Layer 3: the file architecture
23:22 - The memory protocol (add this to AGENTS.md)
26:06 - Retrieval: Track A, A+, and QMD
31:59 - Cost and cache: why memory saves you money
33:33 - The complete config (copy and go)
36:35 - 5 things to remember

---
